Because you're not obligated to cook what someone else wants, especially if you're making a health change. The key is whether you're being reasonable. He's not forcing her to eat healthy; he's just not providing the unhealthy. If she can't cook for herself, then he's not providing food, but he's offered to help her learn. So it's not his fault she can't cook; he's trying to help her become self-sufficient. So NTA.
